This disruption leads to a shared set of downstream phenotypes including congenital muscular dystrophy, brain anomalies, and eye anomalies, characteristic of both disease types A3 and A9.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of pathogenic variants in POMGNT1 or DAG1 with a significantly different functional consequence (e.g., dominant-negative effect) in one disease compared to the other, or the identification of distinct, non-overlapping downstream molecular pathways uniquely affected in each disease type. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism in the dystroglycan glycosylation pathway highlights potential therapeutic targets applicable to both subtypes of muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy. Strategies aimed at restoring or compensating for the aberrant glycosylation process could offer a unified therapeutic approach.
